calls.reason: Contemporary independent reporting (The Decoder, Sept 2024) describes OpenAI and Anthropic as deep in the red, with Anthropic's expected loss far exceeding its revenue. These are forecasts, not realized results, but they clearly point the claim's way.
There is no deadline. Microsoft's 2025 project withdrawals were local and coexisted with growing capex guidance, and no broad end to the AI boom is shown.
This is a conditional forecast, and no evidence establishes frontier-model diminishing returns. NVIDIA's efficiency case for Rubin is a vendor argument, not buyer economics.
The antecedent of a broad AI bubble pop is not established. Reuters reports China's crash but only a 6% Nasdaq drawdown in the US, and Amazon still plans about $200B in capex.
Anthropic's S-1 shows improved operating income and cash flow, but it doesn't isolate chip savings. There is no OpenAI data and no deadline, so the forecast can't yet be called.
The claim is hedged ('I hypothesize') and conditional. No cost-covering repricing by either provider is documented; Cursor's plan change and the Opus 4.5 pricing don't establish the antecedent.
